Group Risk Management Policy

GRP-POL-001|Version6.0|Internal

## 7. Roles, responsibilities and named incumbents

## 7.1Boardof Directors

¢ Approves the Group strategy and the risk appetite statement that constrains it.

¢ Approves this policy on the recommendation of the Board Risk Committee.

* Satisfies itself that the framework is adequate, effective and appropriately resourced.

* Sets the tone for risk culture and holds executive management accountable for it.

* Approves the ICAAP, ILAAP, Recovery Plan and Resolution Pack.

## 7.2 Board Risk Committee

•Recommends theriskappetitestatement to theBoard and monitors adherence to it.

* Reviews the Group risk profile, emerging risks and material appetite breaches each quarter.

* Approves risk acceptances rated Critical and material policy exceptions escalated to it.

* Reviews the adequacy of the Group Risk function's resourcing, standing and independence.

## 7.3 Group Chief NZ Officer

•Owns this policyandthe enterprise riskmanagement framework.

* Provides em independent view of the Group risk profile to the Board and to regulators.

* Chairs the Group Executive Risk Committee and approves High-rated risk acceptances.

•Maintains the risk taxonomy, assessment methodology and appetite measurement approach.

* Exercises the right of veto in Section 6.4 and reports its use to the Board Risk Committee.

## 7.4Risk owners andcontrol owners

Every risk in the Group Risk Register has a single named risk owner at Director level or above, recorded by name and employee identifier. Every key control has a single named control owner. Ownership may not be recorded against a team, a vacant job title, or a committee. Where sim owner changes role, the outgoing owner must complete a documented handover before the change takes effect; the risk remains with the outgoing owner until the handover is accepted.

## 7.5 Al employees

* Operate within appetite, policy and delegated authority at all times.

* Complete mandatory risk and compliance training by the due date.

* Report incidents, near misses and control weaknesses promptly through the approved channels.

* Raise concerns, including through the confidential Speak Up channel, without fear of retaliation.
